title: LeVJEPA: Video Pretraining Without the Asymmetry
hook: Drop the EMA target encoder, the stop-gradient, and the crippled predictor — a single encoder with a provably collapse-free loss matches V-JEPA 2 at up to 20x less compute.
key_points: Self-supervised video methods avoid collapse either by architectural asymmetries (EMA target encoder + stop-gradient + limited predictor) or by pixel reconstruction.
LeVJEPA is the first video encoder trained under LeJEPA's collapse-free objective, which needs neither.
One encoder, one projector: an invariance loss over global and local views of a clip, regularized by SIGReg with a provable no-collapse guarantee, and a single hyperparameter.
Pretraining cost is governed by tokens seen, so uniform random token dropping cuts cost while improving downstream accuracy.
At matched epochs on identical data it matches or surpasses V-JEPA 2 across ViT-S/B/L at 5.6-20.8x less compute.
Against a compute-matched DINOv2 on frames of the same videos, it nearly doubles motion-centric accuracy while approaching it on appearance tasks.
content_html: Video should be a great substrate for visual pretraining — it carries the temporal structure of the physical world for free. It has mostly not been, because it is expensive. Prevailing self-supervised methods either prevent representation collapse with a stack of architectural asymmetries (an EMA target encoder, a stop-gradient, a deliberately weak predictor) or sidestep it by reconstructing masked pixels.
extra_html:
The method

LeVJEPA is the first video encoder trained under LeJEPA's collapse-free objective, which needs neither. A single encoder is trained with an invariance loss over global and local views of a clip, regularized by SIGReg, which excludes collapse with a provable guarantee. The architecture reduces to an encoder plus a projector; the objective reduces to a single hyperparameter.

Two consequences follow. First, cost is governed by how many tokens the encoder observes, so uniform random token dropping makes pretraining much cheaper — and in their experiments simultaneously improves downstream accuracy. Second, with no asymmetry between branches to maintain, the encoder can be trained with block-causal attention at no measurable accuracy cost, so temporal ordering becomes a property of the encoder itself.

Results

At matched epochs on identical data, LeVJEPA matches or surpasses V-JEPA 2 across ViT-S/B/L at 5.6 to 20.8x less pretraining compute. At matched total FLOPs it exceeds the strongest video baseline by 7.6 points on ImageNet-1K while staying competitive on motion-centric benchmarks. Against a compute-matched DINOv2 trained on frames from the same videos, it approaches the image-pretrained encoder on appearance-centric evaluation while nearly doubling its motion-centric accuracy.

The authors' conclusion: once the computational overhead is removed, video becomes a viable — and in several respects preferable — substrate for general-purpose visual pretraining.

related.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words (ViT)
related.hook: Chop an image into patches, treat each like a word, and feed them to a plain Transformer. With enough pretraining data, it matches or beats convolutional networks.

related.title: DINO: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
related.hook: Train a Vision Transformer with no labels at all, and something surprising happens: its attention maps trace out object boundaries on their own.

flashcards.prompt: What is representation collapse, and how do JEPA-style methods usually prevent it?
flashcards.back_html: Collapse is when the encoder maps everything to the same vector, trivially satisfying an invariance loss. Standard fixes use architectural asymmetry — an EMA target encoder, a stop-gradient, and a capacity-limited predictor.

flashcards.prompt: Why does removing branch asymmetry let LeVJEPA use block-causal attention?

choices.text: With no target/student split to keep consistent, temporal ordering can be baked into the single encoder
Block-causal attention is required by the SIGReg regularizer
Causal attention is the only way to avoid collapse without an EMA target

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper reports block-causal attention at no measurable accuracy cost once the architecture reduces to one encoder plus a projector — temporal order becomes a property of the encoder itself.

flashcards.prompt: What makes uniform random token dropping so effective here?
flashcards.back_html: Pretraining cost is governed by how many tokens the encoder sees. Dropping tokens makes that number small while, in their experiments, simultaneously improving downstream accuracy.
